name: Cephalothin
executiveSummary: 1st-generation cephalosporin. Adult: **1–2 g IV every 4–6 h** (max **12 g/day**); surgical prophylaxis **1–2 g**. Pediatrics: **80–150 mg/kg/day** divided every 6–8 h. Alternative to cefazolin in many centers.
indications:
## Indications

- Skin/soft-tissue, respiratory and ear infections by susceptible Gram-positive cocci.
- Perioperative surgical prophylaxis.

## Precautions

- β-lactam allergy. Frequent IV phlebitis.
- Less convenient than cefazolin in many modern protocols — check availability.
- Potential nephrotoxicity with aminoglycosides.

> Darkening at room temperature does not necessarily mean loss of potency (label).

adulto.dose: Treatment: **0.5–2 g IV/IM every 4–6 h** (usual **1 g every 6 h**; severe up to **2 g every 4 h**). Max **12 g/day**. Prophylaxis: **1–2 g** pre-op (± redose by duration).
adulto.administration: IV push 3–5 min (reconstitute ~10 mL) or dilute 100 mL NS/D5W over 30–60 min. IM possible.
adulto.notes: If incomplete dissolution, add 0.2–0.5 mL SW and shake.

pediatrico.dose: **80–150 mg/kg/day** IV divided every 6–8 h (often **100 mg/kg/day**); max **12 g/day**.
pediatrico.administration: IV; conc. up to ~100 mg/mL per card.
pediatrico.notes: Renal adjustment. Avoid unnecessary AG combination.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: ~12 h room temp / ~96 h refrigerated.
- Diluted: ~24 h room temp.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Rash, phlebitis, diarrhea, eosinophilia; rare: leukopenia, nephrotoxicity.
